samples.summary: The triage renderer drops the advisory (non-gating) lens distinction that severity.mjs deliberately encodes, so a non-gating lens's critical/major findings render under "🚫 Blocking" beneath a possibly-green headline.
samples.evidence: `bucketOf` buckets purely on severity+lane, and `renderReviewComment` computes `blocked` only from lenses where `l.gating !== false` (review-comment.mjs ~line 175 in the diff). `severity.mjs::renderSummaryMd` takes an explicit `advisory` flag precisely so "a green check would [not] open with a ❌ that contradicts it" (severity.mjs:130-147), and review-panel.mjs writes `advisory: !blocking` / `conclusion: "success"` for non-gating lenses (review-panel.mjs:2562-2566). In the new layout a non-gating lens raising majors produces `### 🟢 Review panel: looks good` plus `#### 🚫 Blocking (N)` in the same comment, with no marker that those findings do not gate. All lenses in lenses.json are currently `gating: "blocking"`, so the defect is latent today, but the renderer discards a distinction the surrounding design maintains on purpose.

samples.summary: `mergedFrom` wordings are rendered only for blocking findings, so clustered wordings on minor/nit/relocated findings are silently dropped — contradicting the panel's stated invariant and the module's own comment.
samples.evidence: `mergedNote()` is called only from `blockingEvidence()`; `minorRow()` and `relocatedRow()` never call it. The old renderer emitted the "also reported as (N)" fold for EVERY severity section (severity.mjs:75-80), with the rationale that "a collapse nobody can inspect is a silent deletion with extra steps" (severity.mjs:71-74). The new module's own header claims merged wordings are "shown on expand so a reader can see what was merged (never silently dropped)" — true only for blocking rows. The change bills itself as PRESENTATION ONLY / lossless (module header; harness-engineering.md:405), so this is an unmet part of its own stated contract. The preservation test only asserts top-level summaries survive, not mergedFrom.

samples.summary: The blocked/header gate rule now exists in two places: the workflow's inline loop (kept for the fallback path) and renderReviewComment, whose comment claims it was "moved here" — a drift risk the repo's single-source-of-truth style (severity.mjs) usually avoids.
samples.evidence: Workflow lines 539-548 still compute `blocked`/`header` from manifest gating + panel.json; review-comment.mjs re-derives the same rule with the comment "Same decision as the workflow's old inline computation, moved here". Nothing was actually moved — both copies live on. Same pattern for the unverified note (severity.mjs:153-158 vs review-comment.mjs) and the relocated proof line (severity.mjs:112-116 duplicated verbatim in relocatedRow).

samples.summary: `collectLenses` is a second traversal of the `.agent-review` tree alongside `ai-prompt.mjs::collectFindings`, which the same workflow job already runs one step earlier; the verdict.json read/parse/fail-safe logic could be shared.
samples.evidence: ai-prompt.mjs:102-120 defines `collectFindings(reviewDir)` reading `<reviewDir>/<lens>/verdict.json` with identical fail-safe semantics; review-comment.mjs adds `collectLenses(reviewDir, manifest)` doing the same reads plus panel.json. Both are invoked in adjacent steps of agent-review-on-demand.yml.

samples.summary: Design doc overstates the guarantee: it says collapsed sections are dropped past the budget "(blocking findings never are)", but the implementation also drops blocking one-liners under a tight budget, reporting them as "N blocking findings hidden for length".
samples.evidence: harness-engineering.md:403-405 vs review-comment.mjs's `hiddenBlocking` path ("a pathological count still must not exceed the cap — keep as many as fit, count the rest"), exercised by the test "blocking one-liners overflowing the cap are counted, never silently dropped".

samples.summary: Omitting zero-finding and non-applicable lenses removes the only signal of WHICH lenses actually ran; the previous comment listed every lens's ✅/skipped header, so a reader can no longer distinguish "lens passed" from "lens never ran".
samples.evidence: `lensesWithFindings = perLens.filter((l) => l.total > 0)` drives both the headline and every section; a lens with no findings contributes nothing, including no reviewer note (test: "a zero-finding lens contributes no note"). The old body concatenated all six lenses' summary.md, each opening with `✅ <Lens> review: approved …` or a skip note. Documented in harness-engineering.md:403, so intentional — but it is a real loss of coverage information in an advisory review comment.

samples.summary: On a fully clean review the renderer returns "" and the workflow falls back to the OLD verbose per-lens concatenation, so the triage layout is absent in exactly the common green case, and the fallback branch conflates "nothing to say" with "the build step failed".
samples.evidence: `if (lensesWithFindings.length === 0 && erroredCount === 0) return "";` plus the workflow's `if (!region) region = \`${header}\n\n${bodies.join(...)}\``. A zero-finding review therefore still posts six full lens bodies rather than a one-line 🟢 headline.

verdict.reason: The quoted code is genuinely present as described (bucketOf ignores gating at review-comment.mjs:34-42; blocked is gating-filtered at review-comment.mjs:168-171; severity.mjs:139-147 does carry an advisory flag; review-panel.mjs:2562-2568 sets advisory/success for non-gating lenses). But it is not blocking under the design-fit rubric. (a) It cannot manifest: every lens in scripts/agent/lenses/lenses.json is "gating": "blocking" (lines 5,16,26,37,48,59) and collectLenses derives gating only from that manifest (review-comment.mjs:311), so the "green headline + 🚫 Blocking" render is unreachable — the reviewer concedes it is latent. (b) It misses no spec obligation: the canonical design doc docs/design/harness-engineering.md:393-414 specifies this triage layout in detail (headline + every blocking finding first, presentation only) and imposes no advisory/non-gating annotation requirement; no acceptance criterion, Non-Goal, or design-doc gap is cited. (c) It is not duplication or wrong-layer — severity.mjs::renderSummaryMd serves the per-lens check bodies, deliberately untouched (review-comment.mjs:13-17). (d) The entire surface is already declared non-gating: agent-review-on-demand.yml:584 appends "Advisory only — … does not gate merge" to every such comment and the job holds only checks: read (line 172). What is left is a forward-looking consistency preference about propagating a flag no configured lens sets — kind-wise a minor/taste item, which never blocks under this rubric.

verdict.reason: Verified in the tree: mergedNote() in review-comment.mjs is invoked only from blockingEvidence() (line 99), and the renderers for the other buckets — minorRow (105-110) and relocatedRow (114-123) — never emit mergedFrom, while those are the sole renderers for the suggestion/nit (199-211) and relocated (212-218) sections. The case is reachable: clusterFindings is run over the full findings list (review-panel.mjs:2330) and mergeCluster sets mergedFrom unconditionally (685-688), so minor/nit and backlog-lane survivors can carry folded wordings. I looked for a counterexample elsewhere in the consuming channel and found none: agent-review-on-demand.yml:591-593 uses the per-lens summary.md concatenation (severity.mjs::section, which does render the fold at 75-79) only as a fallback when the triage region is empty, and the appended AI-prompt fold is blocking-only by construction (ai-prompt.mjs:11-16, 23-28). This lands in the design-fit lane because the invariant is documented canonically, not just in a code comment: docs/design/harness-engineering.md:561-564 justifies model-free clustering on the grounds that "every collapsed wording rides along in mergedFrom and is rendered". One sub-claim is wrong — severity.mjs::demotedSection (100-126) never rendered mergedFrom, so relocatedRow is at parity — but the minor/nit half is a real loss versus the prior renderer, so the finding stands.
